topic: Are there any particles that behave oppositely to the properties or states of photons?
key_answer: In the standard quantum-field description the photon is its own antiparticle. Opposite helicity, polarization, propagation direction, and OAM labels describe potentially distinguishable states of the same photon species, not a distinct antiphoton.
known_risks: Publisher/DOI landing-page verification remains required before external publication.
A physical photon-state implementation requires quantum-optics review of mode and measurement assumptions.
Charge-conjugation, parity, and time-reversal implementations require quantum-field-theory review.
